cards.title: Two-sided hardness amplification by ODD-MAX-BIT
cards.area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
cards.formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(c>0\) and an integer \(M_0\ge1\) such that, for every \(N\ge1\), every \(M\ge M_0\), and every total Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^N\to\{-1,1\}\), \(\widetilde{\deg}_{1-2^{-cM}}(\operatorname{OMB}_M\circ f)\ge\widetilde{\deg}_{2/3}(f)\)? Here the composition applies the same f separately to M disjoint blocks of N bits, and OMB returns the parity-coded position of the last −1 output. Both approximate degrees in the proposed inequality are ordinary two-sided, pointwise approximate degrees.
cards.why: Tests whether a concrete composition can amplify ordinary polynomial-approximation hardness without a one-sided structural hypothesis. Such a theorem would broaden a mechanism underlying separations in learning, quantum query and communication complexity while preserving a sharp quantitative degree bound.
cards.status_note: Read the original definitions, Theorem 1 and Conjecture 3, and checked the latest ECCC revision and later survey sections on OMB. Searches through 12 September 2026 did not identify a resolution of the all-total-functions, two-sided version with the full degree preserved. The exponent is stated with universal constants, as the quantitative theorem-style interpretation of the source. Searches are not exhaustive and proofs were not independently audited.

cards.definitions:
For a total function \(g:\{- 1,1\}^{t}\to \{- 1,1\}\) and an error parameter \(\eta\in[0,1)\), its \(\eta\)-approximate degree, written \(\tilde\{d\}_{\eta}(g)\), is the least nonnegative integer d for which a real polynomial p in t variables of total degree at most d satisfies |\(p(x)- g(x)|\le \eta\) for every \(x\in \{- 1,1\}^{t}\). Coefficients are arbitrary real numbers, with no bound on their magnitudes, bit representations, monomial count or computation time. Polynomials may be taken multilinear on the Boolean cube by replacing even powers of each variable by 1. A constant function has approximate degree zero. The target is a mathematical degree inequality, not a demand to efficiently construct the polynomial or compute its minimum degree from a succinct representation.

For \(y=(y_{1},\ldots ,y_{M})\in \{- 1,1\}\)ᴹ, define \(j=\max (\{i\in \{1,\ldots ,M\}:y_{i}=- 1\}\cup \{0\})\). Then \(OMB_{M}(y)=- 1\) if j is odd and +1 if j is even. In particular \(OMB_{M}(+1,\ldots ,+1)=+1\). The index runs from 1 to M and “last” means the largest index, matching the primary source. It does not mean parity of the total number of negative inputs. Given disjoint blocks \(x^{1},\ldots ,x^{M}\in \{- 1,1\}\)ᴺ, define (\(OMB_{M}\circ f\))\((x^{1},\ldots ,x^{M})=OMB_{M}(f(x^{1}),\ldots ,f(x^{M}))\). Its domain is the entire cube on MN bits; there are no promises, correlations or overlapping blocks.

The constant c and threshold \(M_{0}\) are independent of f,N,M and the degree. This spells out the uniform exponential-margin interpretation of \(1- 2^{- \Omega (M)}\) in Conjecture 3. Only M tends to infinity in that error expression, and N may vary freely with M. The bound must preserve the entire integer degree \(\tilde\{d\}_{2/3}(f)\), not merely a fixed fraction of it. Equivalently, whenever \(\tilde\{d\}_{2/3}(f)\ge d\) for an integer d, no polynomial of degree less than d may approximate the composition within the stated error. The allowance of a universal threshold \(M_{0}\) expresses the source’s asymptotic notation without asserting a special finite-length constant.

Because outputs are ±1, the number \(1- 2^{- cM}\) is an absolute pointwise approximation error. It is close to 1, not close to zero, and is not a probability that an algorithm makes a mistake. For example, a polynomial satisfying this bound must still have the correct sign everywhere and a nonzero margin at least \(2^{- cM}\), while also staying within the specified error of ±1. Merely requiring the correct sign is threshold degree, a different measure; no fixed margin follows from a threshold representation of unrestricted coefficients.

The already-proved theorem uses positive one-sided approximate degree instead. A positive one-sided \(\eta\)-approximant p satisfies |\(p(x)+1|\le \eta\) when \(f(x)=- 1\) and \(p(x)\ge 1- \eta\) when \(f(x)=+1\), with no upper bound in the second case. Its minimum degree can be strictly smaller than the ordinary two-sided degree. Thus assuming this one-sided degree is at least d is stronger than assuming ordinary approximate degree at least d. Theorem 1 proves the source’s amplification with that stronger hypothesis and error \(1- 2^{- M}\); it does not imply the proposed two-sided-hypothesis statement.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the displayed inequality with constants uniform over all total inner functions and block lengths, or refute the existence of such constants. A negative answer must rule out every proposed universal c and \(M_{0}\), rather than merely one numerical choice of c. A theorem assuming large positive one-sided degree, restricting f to one example, losing a factor in the preserved degree, or asserting only a threshold-degree bound does not settle the stated conjecture.

context_blocks.title: Hardness despite a very weak approximation requirement
context_blocks.text: The proposed composition would retain all of an inner function’s constant-error approximate degree even when the outer approximation error approaches 1 exponentially quickly in the number of blocks. This is a different direction from reducing an error parameter toward zero.

context_blocks.title: The theorem and conjecture have different hypotheses
context_blocks.text: The source proves amplification for positive one-sided approximate degree and explicitly asks whether ordinary two-sided hardness suffices. Conjecture 3 makes that distinction; the saved draft had retained only the sentence introducing it.

context_blocks.title: The outer function is part of the claim
context_blocks.text: The source shows that replacing OMB by OR does not give the same amplification in general. The card keeps OMB’s exact definition and does not replace this question with a generic composition theorem.

context_blocks.title: Later applications do not give this universal extension
context_blocks.text: The 2022 survey discusses particular OMB compositions in applications to threshold circuits and sign-rank. Those specific constructions and guarantees do not establish the all-inner-functions approximate-degree inequality asked here.

cards.context:
The proposed composition would retain all of an inner function’s constant-error approximate degree even when the outer approximation error approaches 1 exponentially quickly in the number of blocks. This is a different direction from reducing an error parameter toward zero.

The source proves amplification for positive one-sided approximate degree and explicitly asks whether ordinary two-sided hardness suffices. Conjecture 3 makes that distinction; the saved draft had retained only the sentence introducing it.

The source shows that replacing OMB by OR does not give the same amplification in general. The card keeps OMB’s exact definition and does not replace this question with a generic composition theorem.

The 2022 survey discusses particular OMB compositions in applications to threshold circuits and sign-rank. Those specific constructions and guarantees do not establish the all-inner-functions approximate-degree inequality asked here.

methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
